cases.reason: 2023's clause adds a constraint the 2002 clause lacks: 15.43.4 RV1 requires a floating-point numeric-edited argument's greatest value to pass an IN-ARITHMETIC-RANGE test (a condition 2002 does not have at all: zero occurrences in the 2002 text). 2002 permits exponent '+999', so PIC +9.9E+999 is a conforming 2002 argument and 2002 RV1 requires the returned value 9.9E+999 (representable in a 2002 standard intermediate, range to 10**1000 - 10**968). The 2023 row's verdict says nothing about that argument (2023 makes it non-conforming). Probe rh3: at --std 2002 under native arithmetic the compiler REFUSES the program with COBOL1660 citing §2023:15.43.4 r1 (also at 2023); rh4: under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD at 2002 it returns +9.9E+999 correctly. Whether the native refusal is licensed by 2002 ('characteristics and representation of the returned value are defined by the implementor', 15.3.1) needs adjudication; it is not licensed by any 2002 rule the diagnostic names. Sibling not in this slice: LOWEST-ALGEBRAIC (2023 15.58.4 r1, same COBOL1660).
